rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nation that ignores its messenger is destroyed; clear signs are sent in messengers’ times to awaken people to their calls.
rows.anchor: If it does not listen to the call of its messenger, it is destroyed by God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God delays punishment to give the disbelievers respite, allowing the truth to reach them fully so they have no excuse for denial.
rows.anchor: This verse states the wisdom behind the delay in punishment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Prophet’s community continues mocking him, God will seize it as He seized earlier communities for the same offense.
rows.anchor: If the Prophet’s (sws) nation also continues to mock at him, it will be seized by God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final yāʾ is omitted from ʿiqāb for rhythmic effect.
rows.anchor: has been dropped for rhythm.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should answer that the partners people invent without proof do not exist and are mere conjecture.
rows.anchor: these deities do not even exist. They are mere conjecture.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers face punishment in this world and a still harsher punishment in the next.
rows.anchor: These people will be faced with God’s punishment in this world and in the next they will encounter an even sterner punishment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only believing monotheists are worthy of Paradise.
rows.anchor: Only His believers who are monotheists are worthy of Paradise.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should not grieve over the people’s rejection of this evident truth.
rows.anchor: the Prophet (sws) should not be sad.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good People of the Book who follow their own scripture rejoice in the revelation given to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: Those among the People of the Book who are good and adhere to their own Book are very happy with the Book

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding statement about being guided further is identified as an established divine practice mentioned elsewhere in the exegesis.
rows.anchor: being guided further. This established practice of God has been referred at a number of instances in this exegesis.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was sent to lead his people from darkness to light and, with God’s help, freed them from Pharaoh’s oppression.
rows.anchor: he was also sent to bring out his people from darkness to light. Thus he fulfilled this responsibility and with God’s help he liberated them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells Moses that gratitude brings further blessing, while ingratitude brings stern punishment.
rows.anchor: if he gives due regard to God’s favour and remains grateful, he will be blessed further. On the other hand, if he is ungrateful, he will face God’s stern punishment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder warns contemporary Jews who backed Quraysh against Islam and had forgotten Abraham’s and Moses’ teachings.
rows.anchor: The purpose of this reminder was to warn the Jews who had stared to openly support the Quraysh against Islam.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ signs are his staff and the white hand, which the Qur’an discusses in detail elsewhere.
rows.anchor: The signs mentioned in this verse refer to the staff and to white hand of Moses (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Days” here means memorable historical days; ayyām Allāh are occasions when God punished disobedient nations and rescued faithful people from oppression, like the expression for Arab wars.
rows.anchor: refers to the historic days in which the Almighty punished disobedient nations and saved His faithful servants from their aggression and oppression.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses and his people suffered Pharaoh’s oppression before God destroyed Pharaoh’s followers and saved Israel; the verse applies this pattern to Muslims’ current trial, where steadfastness leads to success and gratitude.
rows.anchor: God ultimately destroyed the Pharaoh and his followers and saved the Israelites. The last part of the verse implies that Muslims too are facing a trial.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word āl can mean followers as well as family.
rows.anchor: not only refers to family and but also to followers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ post-liberation speech reminds Israel that it passed a severe trial only through God’s help and should remain grateful rather than repeat the sins that led to slavery.
rows.anchor: they had successfully passed through a very tough trial merely because of God’s help. Hence they should keep this favour of God in mind

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speech reminds Israelites in the Prophet’s time that they forgot Moses’ advice, followed Satan again, and would bring doom on themselves by evading Islam.
rows.anchor: they have forgotten the advice of Moses (sws) and are once again following the footsteps of Satan. This attitude of evasion from Islam would result in their own doom.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse too is intended to warn the Israelites living in the Prophet’s time.
rows.anchor: This verse too is meant to warn the Israelites of the times of the Prophet (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrah al-Ḥijr expands the warning to Quraysh and assurance to the Prophet that closed the preceding sūrah.
rows.anchor: the assurance sounded to the Prophet (sws) at the end of the previous sūrah is dilated upon in this sūrah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is proof in itself and needs no external miracle; rejecters will later regret refusing it.
rows.anchor: the Qur’ ān is a proof in itself and does not need any external sign or miracle for its validation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Demanding angels and rejecting messengers repeat earlier nations’ behavior; even demanded miracles will not reform these people, so the Prophet should leave them to themselves.
rows.anchor: Even if they are shown the miracles they demand, they are not going to mend their ways. So, he should leave them to themselves.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fixed time is set for the nation’s destruction; when angels arrive, they execute God’s verdict and no respite follows, while God protects the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: A day has been fixed for the destruction of this nation. When this time expires, God’s torment will visit it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier nations met their fate, and even the greatest miracles would not persuade these rejecters because they would invent an excuse.
rows.anchor: the greatest of miracles will not be able to convince these people. If they see them, they will still have an excuse of rejection.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky, stars, earth’s varied produce, winds, and rain are signs that validate the Qur’an’s call and should teach people without needing a miracle.
rows.anchor: The sky and its dazzling stars, the earth and the diversity of its produce, the winds and the rain they send sound are portrayed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of Adam’s creation and Satan’s response is introduced to explain the real reason people disbelieve.
rows.anchor: The purpose is to delineate the real reason behind the

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People disbelieve because Satan and his progeny deceive them, not because the Prophet lacks proof; the account also points to the ultimate fate of disbelief and the success of the pious who resist Satan.
rows.anchor: Another purpose was to remind the addressees of the ultimate fate of this disbelief to which they were lured by Satan and his progeny.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ visit to Abraham shows God’s mercy and vengeance: the angels bringing news of a son also destroyed Lot’s people.
rows.anchor: The very angels that came to Abraham (sws) with the glad tidings of a son were responsible to bring destruction upon the nation of Lot (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers should learn from the overturned settlements of Lot’s people that they pass; their demand for angels should recall that angels arrived for Lot with the punishment.
rows.anchor: when angels do come, they come in the manner they came to Lot’s nation: after their arrival, God’s punishment descends.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fates of Shuʿayb’s and Ṣāliḥ’s peoples are recalled; Quraysh passed their remains on trade journeys, where the signs of evildoers’ fate could be seen at every step.
rows.anchor: Like the nation of Lot (sws), the Quraysh would pass by the remains of these nations too in their trade journeys.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh should open their eyes to the signs around them instead of waiting to experience their own fate.
rows.anchor: if they have a keen eye, the signs of the fate of the miscreants can be seen at every step.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to graciously ignore the deniers, since they will meet their fate and the Qur’an’s treasure is sufficient; he should glorify God and pray, and truth will soon become clear.
rows.anchor: The great treasure of the Qur’ān the Almighty has blessed him with is sufficient for him. In its presence, he needs nothing else.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word for wind refers to seasonal winds that load clouds with water and bring rain.
rows.anchor: laden and send down rain.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain is part of God’s providential system: only He can send winds to gather clouds and produce life-giving water, a merciful provision humans cannot store and dispense independently.
rows.anchor: It is He alone Who sends forth seasonal winds which gather clouds and make them produce rain.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God alone gives life and death, He alone inherits, guards, and protects the earth’s inhabitants; hope in anyone else is mere conjecture.
rows.anchor: no one has any authority to give life and death, no one has any right in the inheritance of the inhabitants

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s wisdom entails a Day of Judgement, and His knowledge means no one escapes observation and no deed is unknown to Him.
rows.anchor: The fact that He is wise entails that He will bring about a Day of Judgement and the fact that He is knowledgeable means that neither can anyone be beyond His observation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Adam and Satan account shows that disbelievers reject the Messenger because Satan’s progeny deceived them, rather than because proof or demanded miracles were lacking.
rows.anchor: the actual reason is that they have been deceived by the progeny of Satan.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan had threatened to mislead people when ordered to prostrate to Adam and said he would lead them astray if given the opportunity.
rows.anchor: He had threatened to lead people astray at the time he was asked to prostrate before Adam (sws).
